message.reasoning_content: We need to determine crimes based on facts. The facts: Li XX, severe disease, wants revenge. On Sep 29 2014, he opened gas stove, intended to cause gas explosion by dialing phone to create spark. Neighbor discovered, called police, closed gas, no explosion. Next day, he went with a knife to a commercial area, stabbed 20 people, causing various injuries (some heavy, some light). He was subdued. So crimes: attempted arson? Actually causing explosion: using gas to cause explosion is a dangerous act. In Chinese criminal law, causing explosion is "放火罪" (arson) or "危害公共安全罪" (endangering public safety). Specifically, "以危险方法危害公共安全罪" (dangerous means endangering public safety) includes using explosives, dangerous chemicals, etc. Gas explosion attempt could be "放火罪" if fire, but here it's gas explosion. Could be "以危险方法危害公共安全罪" (dangerous means endangering public safety). Also "故意伤害罪" for stabbing many people. The injuries: heavy, light, minor. So multiple counts of intentional injury. Possibly "故意伤害罪" (intentional injury). Also "非法持有、私藏枪支"? No. Also "非法制造、买卖、运输、储存危险物质"? Not. So likely crimes: "以危险方法危害公共安全罪" (dangerous method endangering public safety) and "故意伤害罪". In examples, they sometimes list "故意伤害" as a single crime even with multiple victims. So answer: [罪名]以危险方法危害公共安全罪;故意伤害<eoa>. However the examples sometimes use "故意伤害" alone. Also "放火罪" maybe. But gas explosion attempt is not fire but explosion. Chinese law: Article 115 of Criminal Law: "以危险方法危害公共安全罪" includes "放火、爆炸、投放危险物质". So yes. So answer: [罪名]以危险方法危害公共安全罪;故意伤害<eoa>.
